The patient is a 15-year-old male with obesity, mild persistent asthma, and atopic dermatitis, previously evaluated in 2020 and 2021 for left hip, thigh, and knee pain, who presents with new-onset right thigh and groin discomfort.
He first noticed a dull ache after participating in a weekend soccer game, which he attributed to overexertion.
The pain has not resolved with rest or over-the-counter analgesics, and he has been avoiding physical activity at school.
His mother has noticed a progressive limp, particularly when he climbs stairs.
He also mentions feeling more tired than usual and says he sometimes feels stiffness in the mornings, although this usually improves within an hour.
There is no history of trauma, recent travel, rashes, or fever.
